notes.title: Project II: Silent Valley | Director’s Q&A | Part 1
notes.notes: [p][b]Q1. What kind of game is this?[/b][/p][p]This is a [i]serious-narrative[/i] game. Players will take on the role of the protagonist, Hierophan Hemersfield—a workaholic military officer who, while stationed at the Silent Valley base, unexpectedly discovers his emotional attraction toward a “weapon-being,” a lifeform that challenges conventional human notions of sexuality. A significant portion of the story explores the fundamental differences between “weapon-beings” and the classic brainwashed killing machines in dystopian fiction.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q2. Is there romance? Why is the game single-ending?[/b][/p][p]There are no romance options or branching love interests. The main couple is fixed: Officer Hierophan × the weapon-being Osprey. Other characters also have their own relationship arcs, including lesbian and heterosexual dynamics. The writer believes that a single-ending structure allows for a more focused and in-depth narrative, enabling the story to be told with greater emotional and thematic clarity.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q3. What platforms will it be on? Will there be a demo? How much will it cost?[/b][/p][p]The game will be released on [b]Steam[/b], compatible with both [b]Windows[/b] and [b]macOS[/b]. It is scheduled for release in [b]Q4 of 2025[/b], with a [b]demo available during Steam’s October Next Fest[/b]. The final price is expected to be [b]USD 5–6[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q4. I haven’t played [i]Chicago Project[/i]. Will that affect my experience?[/b][/p][p]Not at all! [i]Project II: Silent Valley[/i] and [i]Chicago Project[/i] share the same universe, but they’re set 25 years apart—[i]Silent Valley[/i] takes place earlier in the timeline and can be considered a prequel.[/p][p][i]Cyrivan:[/i] Chicago Project was a story-driven puzzle game. While the narrative was well-received, its gameplay design faced criticism. That’s why this time we’ve moved away from puzzle mechanics, focusing instead on [b]visual novel storytelling[/b], [b]walking sim exploration[/b], and a [b]newly designed card-based battle system[/b]—aiming for a better balance between story and gameplay.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q5. What’s the music in the first teaser PV?[/b][/p][p][i]Cyrivan:[/i] That’s our original soundtrack piece, [b]“Living Legacy”[/b]![/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q6. How long is the game? Is the card battle system difficult?[/b][/p][p]The game runs approximately [b]4–7 hours[/b], featuring over [b]100,000 words of text[/b], [b]28 maps[/b], and more than [b]30 high-quality Live2D CGs[/b]. The card battle system does not emphasize progression; players will start with some of the strongest cards available. The core challenge lies in adapting to increasingly complex battle scenarios. If you lose a match, you can choose to skip it—ensuring smooth narrative progression without interruption.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p]
